text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - Britain's leading stock index finished at a record closing high for the second successive day as investors poured into banking, retail and pharmaceutical stocks that are insulated from the pound's strength. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,899.3, up 41.9 points or 0.86 percent.
FRANKFURT - German stocks ended market dealings with modest losses as the market took a small breather from sharp gains Monday but still found some strength from the dollar trading above 1.79 marks.
The 30-share DAX ended the session down 3.06 points at 4,121.13 points, while the IBIS DAX finished at 4,124.37.
PARIS - French stocks closed with a gain, supported by the dollar, which set fresh highs in the afternoon, dealers said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,950.70, up 9.11 points, or 0.31 percent.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended little changed in quiet trade, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5,844.7, down 1.1 points, or 0.02 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended with moderate losses with prices eroded by profit-taking in the wake of a sharp rise the previous day, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,069.41, down 159.31 points, or 0.79 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks rallied to a new record close, chiefly on momentum buying in index heavyweights HSBC Holdings Plc and Hongkong Telecom, but brokers warned many key stocks lagged the rally. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,487.24, up 116.30 points or 0.76 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold stocks ended lower after the bullion price failed to escape its weak levels, while industrial shares finished firm after a slow start, dealers said. The All-Share index closed at 7,390.7, up 10.1 points, or 0.14 percent. The All-Gold index closed at 976.3, down 23.3 points, or 2.33 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,885.7, up 43.2 points, or 0.49 percent.
